qualification: Review of the two proposed event ABI files, their exact five original operation bodies, one-member recipe projection, provenance and bounded native producer/bootstrap analysis. This does not admit a composite build, install process hooks, establish runtime behavior, or release any Main source hold.

body_review.finding: Same genuine published-controller lookup and registry call. Null returns the separate static zero byte; this byte is not a category-registry index. Original producer cache and process lifetime constraints remain outside the raw entry.

The original int32 argument count and uint64 payload representation are retained. Up to two actual native ConvertableToTraceFormat pointers are adopted by unique_ptr before global lookup. Null controller returns zero and destroys the local owned convertibles under both admission scopes.
Same adoption/null semantics and exact timestamped controller operation; no guest conversion or allocation substitute was introduced.
Same actual native ownership transfer before resolving the published Agent. The Node tracing controller receives metadata if present; otherwise local owners are destroyed synchronously.

The candidate matches the exact original duration macro expanded only at its original destructor call. The p_data_ and enabled-category-byte guard belongs to ScopedTracer and is explicitly retained as a future producer responsibility, not claimed inside this raw entry.

admission_and_lifetime_review: Every body begins with DiagnosticContextScope diagnostic(context), then AllocationScope allocation(memory_owner), with exactly one of each. Reverse destruction keeps the diagnostic context through convertible and allocation-scope teardown. No new context or scope is stored, queued or passed to a delayed guest callback.

The supplied memory owner remains a nonnull live owner for the selected process Agent/controller. This is an explicit native caller precondition; the two raw scope declarations do not prove that future callers satisfy it.

Main DiagnosticContextScope header 7EA7700F is byte-identical to the existing contained composition copy. The standalone donor currently lacks that live header; the packet's composite diagnostic/fatal/build dependency remains open and is not silently treated as installed.

The current controller moves accepted convertibles into TraceObject only on the original recording/buffer path. The native writer formats genuine ConvertableToTraceFormat objects later. Header contracts retain native owned data and ordinary long-lived name/string pointers; FLAG_COPY and COPY_STRING remain distinct.
Native standard allocation uses the existing pi_simd scope and per-block retained native owner. The proposed entries add no allocator, guest JSON proxy, fake trace store, or new failure fallback.

bootstrap_analysis_review.authority: src/node_v8_platform-inl.h:23-62 and its full Initialize/Dispose bodies; current native_node_tracing_controller.cpp
bootstrap_analysis_review.finding: Process observer metadata, first-enabled self-removal, and unreachable OnTraceDisabled are mapped correctly. Registration can call OnTraceEnabled immediately after releasing the controller mutex, so the observer must be fully formed before registration.

The analysis preserves initialized state, Agent construction, global publication, process observer registration, default client/optional tracing start, and only then platform threads. Teardown clears global publication, resets the file client, shuts down/deletes the platform, destroys Agent, then observer; the allocation owner must outlive the complete sequence.

The distinct Environment observer retains owns_process_state, can_call_into_js, principal realm, actual trace-category callback, native handle scope and verbose exception behavior. Registration/begin and observer-removal/end ordering are correctly separated from process observer behavior.

The future genuine native value/process-metadata owner is accurately scoped. Original I18N selection, string-name assumptions, double formatting, AsyncWrap ID-to-int narrowing, native immutable versions/release values, process-title growth/error behavior, and title metadata ordering remain explicit obligations.
